skill.name: agent-browser
skill.description: Automate browser sessions through inference.sh with element refs, page interactions, screenshots, video recording, proxy options, and JavaScript execution.
skill.summary: Browser automation helper for web navigation, testing, capture, and extraction workflows.
skill.author: inference-sh-8

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown syntax, visible shell examples, placeholder URLs, relative documentation links, and /dev/null redirection. Confirmed risks include the remote installer piped to shell, advertised screen capture and file upload capabilities, SOCKS proxy support, cookie extraction guidance, proxy-based rate limit avoidance, and automated authentication handling.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly to sh in the quick start.
remediation.suggestion: Replace it with reviewed package manager instructions or a download-and-verify flow that users run after inspecting the installer.

remediation.issue: Documentation shows extracting cookies from authenticated sessions.
remediation.suggestion: Remove cookie extraction examples or restrict them to owned test systems with redaction and no logging of session data.

remediation.issue: Proxy documentation promotes rate limit avoidance.
remediation.suggestion: Remove bypass language and frame proxy use around authorized geo-testing, corporate access, and compliance with target site limits.

remediation.issue: Screenshots, videos, and file uploads can expose sensitive data.
remediation.suggestion: Add consent, redaction, and data handling warnings before capture, recording, and upload workflows.

remediation.issue: Authentication examples include OAuth, credentials, and TOTP automation.
remediation.suggestion: Limit examples to test accounts, avoid MFA bypass framing, and require authorized use with secrets kept out of logs.

content.user_title: Automate Browser Workflows with Agent Browser
content.value_statement: Manual browser tasks slow down research, testing, and form workflows. This skill uses inference.sh sessions to navigate pages, interact with elements, capture evidence, and extract page content.
actual_capabilities: Opens browser sessions and returns page URL, title, element refs, and screenshots.
Clicks, fills, types, selects, scrolls, uploads files, and navigates through element refs.
Captures viewport or full page screenshots and optional session videos.
Runs JavaScript in the current page to extract text, links, or structured page data.
Routes browser sessions through HTTP, HTTPS, or SOCKS proxies when configured.
Provides shell templates for forms, authenticated sessions, and page capture workflows.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh CLI, an account, and network access to target websites.
Element refs can change after navigation, form submission, or dynamic page updates.
Screenshots and videos can expose sensitive page data if used on private sessions.
Automation must follow site terms, rate limits, and user authorization requirements.

use_cases.title: Test Web Flows
use_cases.description: Run repeatable browser actions, capture screenshots, and record videos for failed test cases.

use_cases.title: Extract Page Content
use_cases.description: Open public pages, collect visible text, save links, and document the page state.

use_cases.title: Document Product Workflows
use_cases.description: Record guided browser sessions and capture screenshots for help articles or process reviews.

prompt_templates.title: Open and Inspect a Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Open this URL with agent-browser. Summarize the page title, visible form fields, main links, and available buttons.

prompt_templates.title: Fill a Simple Form
prompt_templates.prompt: Use agent-browser to inspect this form. Fill the fields I provide, submit it, and report the confirmation state.

prompt_templates.title: Capture Evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Navigate this workflow with agent-browser. Take a full page screenshot at each major step and describe what changed.

prompt_templates.title: Extract Structured Page Data
prompt_templates.prompt: Use agent-browser to open these pages, extract visible text and links, and compare the results in a concise table.

output_examples.input: Inspect a public landing page and list its interactive elements.
output_examples.output: The page opened successfully. It includes a search field, pricing link, documentation link, and sign-in button.

output_examples.input: Submit a contact form with approved test data.
output_examples.output: The form was filled and submitted. The final page displayed a thank-you message and no validation errors.

output_examples.input: Capture a product settings workflow for documentation.
output_examples.output: Screenshots were captured for the settings page, edit action, save action, and final confirmation state.

best_practices: Use only sites and accounts where you have clear authorization.
Re-snapshot after navigation or dynamic updates before using element refs again.
Disable video recording when pages may contain passwords, tokens, or private data.
anti_patterns: Do not use proxy rotation to bypass site limits or access controls.
Do not print, store, or share cookies, passwords, or one-time codes.
Do not run the remote install command without reviewing the installer source.

faq.question: What does this skill automate?
faq.answer: It automates browser navigation, element interaction, screenshots, video capture, proxy configuration, and page data extraction.

faq.question: Does it require inference.sh?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples use the inference.sh CLI and the hosted agent-browser application.

faq.question: Can it work with authenticated pages?
faq.answer: Yes, but use only authorized accounts and avoid recording or logging sensitive authentication data.

faq.question: Why do element refs change?
faq.answer: Refs are generated from the current page state. Navigation or dynamic changes can assign the same ref to a new element.

faq.question: Can it record videos?
faq.answer: Yes. Video recording is session based and becomes available when the browser session closes.

faq.question: Is proxy use supported?
faq.answer: Yes. The documentation includes HTTP, HTTPS, and SOCKS proxy options, which should be used only for authorized purposes.
